text: You know the Statue of Liberty, but almost 20 years before New York, Egypt said no to her.
Rewind to the 1860s, Bartoldi pitches Egypt a giant woman with a light for the new Suez Canal.
Magnificent. Too expensive. No, so Bartoldi reworks it. Same big lady.
New continent. So who pays? France pays for the statue. America pays for the stand.
By 1884, she's finished in Paris, poking above the rooftops.
Imagine that as your neighbor, her iron skeleton, designed by Gustave Eiffel.
Then Paris kicks her apart, about 350 pieces, 214 crates, across the Atlantic.
Spoiler, New York's Stand Fund has about $3,000.
So how do you finish her?
newspaper owner Joseph Pulitzer promises to print every donor's name, any amount.
About a hundred and twenty thousand people chip in. Most gifts are under one
dollar. France gave her a body. Ordinary Americans gave her somewhere to stand.
She's unveiled on October 28th 1886, 140 years ago. And the twist? Her island is
New York. The water around it. New Jersey. Lovely statue. Standing in my water.
Pitched to Egypt. Built in Paris. Paid in coins. Standing in New Jersey. Very
American. This is Boogle. Follow for more geography fun facts.
